The Viewport Size Simulator renders web content in an iframe at specific viewport dimensions, including device pixel ratio (DPR). It simulates how pages appear on different devices by setting both the CSS viewport size and the pixel density, affecting how CSS media queries, images, and font rendering behave.

content.text: DPR affects how CSS pixels map to physical pixels. A 375px viewport at 3x DPR (iPhone) renders differently than at 1x DPR. This tool simulates both dimensions for accurate responsive testing.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.subHeading: Why does DPR matter?

content.text: Higher DPR means more physical pixels per CSS pixel. Images, borders, and text render sharper at 2x/3x. Media queries use CSS pixels, not physical pixels, so DPR doesn't change layout — only rendering quality.
